title: About me
paragraphs: Production engineer by training, product manager by calling, with a technical detour that made all the difference.

I started in 2016 writing code and building web solutions. I learned what it means to ship software to production, debug at 11 PM, and understand that "it works on my machine" isn't shipping. That experience gave me something I've never lost: the ability to speak the same language as the engineering team.

From there, I moved into strategic planning at a holding company (Grupo Euphoria), where I learned to think in systems: how departments connect, how decisions in one area impact another, and how to translate strategy into execution across 10 different companies.

Then I went into BI, where I learned that data without context is useless. Next came PO, where I learned that roadmap without discovery is guessing. I evolved to PM, where I realized that product without metrics is hope. And I reached Senior PM, where I understood that none of this works without clear communication and stakeholder alignment.
What ties it all together: each phase gave me a layer that the next one needed. Code gave me technical fluency. Strategy gave me systems thinking. Data gave me rigor. Product brought it all together.

Today, my focus is at the intersection of AI, data, and product strategy. I thrive in ambiguous environments, embrace complexity, and believe the best version of a PM is one who makes the team around them better.
insightBox: When an engineer explains a technical trade-off to me, I understand. Not because I read about it, but because I've lived it. When the team debates an architectural decision, I can contribute, not just listen. At Mogno AI, this fluency allowed me to structure technical validation tests in hours and dialogue with engineering without intermediaries. In a market where most PMs depend on the tech lead for any technical decision, I can operate with significant autonomy.
